result.reasoning:
I could not refute it: the cancellation is reachable on one of the seven inputs this batch actually fed the kernel, and there it changes the factor far beyond the noise band. But the reporter's mechanism, blast radius and primary fix are all wrong, which changes what has to be fixed and what has to be re-run.

1. MECHANISM IS NOT MAGNITUDE (reporter is wrong). The float32 relative error of (s2/n - mu*mu) depends only on the coefficient of variation sigma/mu of the expanding window, not on the absolute magnitude. Measured (tmp/review/refute_zexp_cancel/t2.py, 400x241 rows, float32): at CV=1.0 the median relative z error is 6.4e-8 at magnitude 1e2, 6.3e-8 at 1e6 and 6.6e-8 at 1e8 — identical. Onset is CV<=3e-3 (median 3e-3), catastrophic below CV~3e-4 (>65% of cells wrong by >10%). So "large-magnitude inputs" / the cross_ema comment about Amt at 1e8-1e9 is the wrong gate, and 1e16 with 1% noise is fine in float32 for exactly that reason (6e-4 relative, not a research-level error).

2. ALL SEVEN ACTUAL CALL SITES, measured on realistic A-share minute panels in float32 vs an exact float64 Welford reference (tmp/review/refute_zexp_cancel/t3.py). Columns = within-day CV, p99 relative z error, fraction of cells wrong by >1%:
   - Ret — runs/F102_kurt_autocorr/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_izse60, runs/F109_erm_mag_gap_5m_tsm20/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_spine_izexp, runs/F113_nested_tsmax_demean/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_g6_inz: CV 26, 1.6e-7, 0.00000. Ret is centred on zero, i.e. the opposite regime from cancellation.
   - log(Volume) — runs/F110_ret_fair_log/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_causal_mask_rev: CV 0.074, 4.0e-5, 0.00000.
   - Amt — runs/F103_amt_dw_decay/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_A_inzs: CV 1.26, 1.7e-6, 0.00000.
   - Volume[31:211] — runs/F115_all_tide_mean_30/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_causal_z: CV 1.14, 1.6e-6, 0.00000.
   - Close — runs/F108_max_ntkurt_close/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_zexp_slow: CV 6.0e-3 (p1 = 0), p99 7.1e+5, 0.16492.
   So the two inputs the reporter singles out (Amt, Volume) are precisely the immune ones, and the one genuinely broken input is Close — magnitude 2-120 CNY, which the reporter never mentions. Close is affected not because it is large but because A-share minute Close sits on the 0.01 tick grid, so the expanding window at small n (the gate is n>=5) is routinely flat to within 1-2 ticks, i.e. CV 1e-5..1e-4.

3. NOTHING ALREADY REPORTED MOVES. The only in_zscore_expand candidates cited in a written conclusion are h3_causal_mask_rev (handoff/F110_ret_fair_log/STATE.md, notes/F110_ret_fair_log/state.md), h3_spine_izexp (handoff/F109_erm_mag_gap_5m_tsm20/results/verdict.json) and h3_causal_z (handoff/F115_all_tide_mean_30/results/verdict.json, finding LF6 on lookahead-into-indices) — all three on log(Volume), Ret and minute Volume, all immune at <=4e-5. h3_zexp_slow appears in no conclusion file: grep finds it only inside two agent transcripts, and only in a "25/25 parse" OK list. It was also not promoted into runs/F108_max_ntkurt_close/sweepfinal_s3.json (8 variants: v_base, k_known, k_known_xfrozen, h3_stdamt_xfroz, seg_lowliq_m, sub_A_nt_ts_var, h3_scr_dbl, z_known_excl_flatrun). Every sweep_s3 landed 17:29-18:25 on 10-05, after every notes/*/state.md, synthesis.md and verdict.json (13:47-17:12), so no round has consumed any s3 number yet.

4. BUT THE ONE AFFECTED SCREENING ROW IS WRONG BY MUCH MORE THAN THE NOISE BAND, so it cannot be waved through for the next F108 round. End-to-end on the real chain cross_mean(day_max(abs_(in_zscore_expand(Close))),30) with the locked hl_long=20 and partura.books.smoothed + top 10% (tmp/review/refute_zexp_cancel/t6.py, 200 stocks x 120 days, plain tick-rounded random walk, no artificial limit-up days): current kernel vs float64 kernel give a mean cross-sectional rank correlation of 0.088 and a mean top-decile overlap of 0.484 (worst day 0.250); 7.3% of stock-days have day_max(abs z) wrong by >2x, 9.3% by >1e6 in the t3 panel. books.py EMAs the RAW signal before ranking (smoothed -> long_short_weights), so a single 1e7 cell dominates that stock's rank for ~20 days instead of being absorbed by a rank transform. The reported train_long sharpe 0.922 / valid_long -0.411 / utrain_long 0.624 for h3_zexp_slow are therefore numbers for a different factor — in effect "did this stock have a flat-tick stretch" — not for the hypothesis that was written ("expanding window removes the 30-minute window degree of freedom").

5. THE SUGGESTED FIX IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY AND ONLY ACCIDENTALLY ADEQUATE. The reporter's own headline example is stated to fail "in both float32 and float64", yet their primary recommendation is the float64 upcast. I confirmed the ramp still returns 14500000000.0 in float64 against an exact 1.675246731754682. For the real input the upcast happens to be enough (float64 two-pass on the realistic Close panel: p99 relative error 2.3e-4, zero cells >1%, day_max ratio exactly 1.000 at p99; float64 two-pass only breaks at CV<=1e-7, which no minute field reaches), but shipping it would leave the kernel with a 1e-7-CV cliff and would not reproduce the reporter's own repro. The reporter's parenthetical second option (centre before squaring) is the one to ship, and it is a one-line vectorised change — no Welford loop needed.

Residual uncertainty: I have no local store (no dtfield_*.npy anywhere under either repo), so the Close numbers come from simulated tick-grid minute paths rather than the real cube. The gating threshold (CV<=3e-3) and the immunity of Ret/log(Volume)/Amt/Volume are measured and hold across four orders of magnitude, so the mapping of which call sites are affected is solid; only the exact affected fraction for Close is simulated. Adjusted (fuhquan) prices would not change this, since a multiplicative adjustment preserves flat stretches.

result.corrected_fix:
Do NOT ship the reporter's primary suggestion (cast to float64 before the cumsums and cast back). It leaves the two-pass formula in place, so it still fails the reporter's own repro — float64 two-pass returns 14500000000.0 on x[t]=1e9+t — and only works on the real input by accident, with a cliff at CV~1e-7.

Ship the reporter's parenthetical option instead: centre before squaring. It needs no Welford loop and keeps the vectorised cumsum, because the z-score is invariant to an additive per-row shift. In /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:630-641, replace the body of in_zscore_expand with:

    x0 = _f(x)
    x64 = x0.to(torch.float64)
    ok = torch.isfinite(x64)
    n = torch.cumsum(ok.to(x64.dtype), -1)
    idx = torch.argmax(ok.to(torch.int8), -1, keepdim=True)          # first finite minute
    shift = torch.where(ok.any(-1, keepdim=True), x64.gather(-1, idx),
                        torch.zeros_like(idx, dtype=x64.dtype))
    y = torch.where(ok, x64 - shift, torch.zeros_like(x64))
    s1, s2 = torch.cumsum(y, -1), torch.cumsum(y * y, -1)
    mu = s1 / n.clamp(min=1)
    var = (s2 / n.clamp(min=1) - mu * mu).clamp(min=0)
    z = torch.where(ok & (n >= 5), (y - mu) / (torch.sqrt(var) + EPS), torch.full_like(x64, NAN))
    return z.to(x0.dtype)

Two things this must not break, both checked in t7.py: the shift is the FIRST FINITE minute (not the row mean, which would reintroduce a full pass and is not available causally in spirit), and after shifting the expanding mean is O(sigma) rather than O(mu), so s2/n - mu*mu no longer subtracts two O(mu^2) terms. Verified: ramp exact to 2.6e-16 in float64; realistic tick-grid Close in float32 max relative error 6.0e-8 with day_max(abs z) ratio exactly 1.000000; no regression on Ret, log(Volume), Amt or minute Volume (all <=6.0e-8). The float64 accumulation is also what cross_ema in the same file already does, so it is consistent with the file's own convention; the `.to(x0.dtype)` at the end keeps the engine's float32 node-exit contract (alphacube/engine/kernels.py:35).

Re-run scope after the fix — only one row changes, and it is unconsumed: runs/F108_max_ntkurt_close/sweep_s3.json:results/h3_zexp_slow (cross_mean(day_max(abs_(in_zscore_expand(Close))),30)) must be re-run before the next F108 round reads it, and its current train/valid/utrain long sharpes 0.922 / -0.411 / 0.624 should be treated as void. The other six call sites (F102 h3_izse60, F103 h3_A_inzs, F109 h3_spine_izexp, F110 h3_causal_mask_rev, F113 h3_g6_inz, F115 h3_causal_z) do not need re-running: their inputs sit 1-4 orders of magnitude above the onset CV, measured p99 error <=4e-5. In particular the LF6 finding in handoff/F115_all_tide_mean_30/results/verdict.json and the F110 STATE.md line both stand unchanged.

Secondary note, not part of this defect but adjacent: `in_zscore_expand(Close)` on A-share minute data has a genuine degenerate exit even with exact arithmetic — on a day whose first minutes are flat to the tick the true std is one tick, so z legitimately reaches sqrt(n-1) ~ 15 at n>=5. If F108 re-runs this candidate, the n>=5 gate is the thing to question (a higher gate, or a floor on the denominator proportional to the tick size), not just the dtype.
